questions.question:
Read the following statements carefully and choose the correct statements.
(i) The vapour pressure of a liquid decreases with increase of temperature.
(ii) The liquid boils at the temperature at which its vapour pressure is equal to the atmospheric pressure.
(iii) Vapour pressure of the solvent decreases in the presence of non-volatile solute.
(iv) Vapour pressure of the pure solvent and solution is a function of temperature.
questions.explanation:
(i) The vapor pressure of a liquid decreases with an increase in temperature. 
This statement is incorrect. Vapor pressure increases with increasing temperature. Higher temperatures provide more kinetic energy to the liquid molecules, allowing them to escape into the gas phase more readily. 
(ii) The liquid boils at the temperature at which its vapour pressure is equal to the atmospheric pressure. 
This statement is correct. Boiling occurs when the vapor pressure of the liquid equals the surrounding pressure (usually atmospheric pressure).
(iii) Vapor pressure of the solvent decreases in the presence of a non-volatile solute. 
This statement is correct. This is known as Raoult's Law. A non-volatile solute reduces the number of solvent molecules at the surface of the liquid, hindering their escape into the vapor phase and thus lowering the vapor pressure. 
(iv) Vapor pressure of the pure solvent and solution is a function of temperature. 
This statement is correct. As discussed in statement (i), temperature directly affects vapor pressure for both pure solvents and solutions.
